thread.title: Services Called 'Next Paradigm Shift' For Apple Stock

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Services Called 'Next Paradigm Shift' For Apple Stock
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) investors are beginning to value the company more as a services provider and less as a smartphone maker, a Wall Street analyst said Friday.
X "The recent move higher in shares of Apple is likely an early reflection of this emerging paradigm shift," Gene Munster, managing partner at Loup Ventures, said in a blog post .
Shares slipped 0.4% to close at 188.59 on the stock market today . On Thursday, the stock hit a record high of 190.37, after rising for nine consecutive trading days .
"As Apple's market cap approaches $1 trillion, it begs the question: Can shares move higher?" Munster wrote. Apple stock appears "well positioned for future appreciation based on a longer-term, more sustainable investing paradigm," he said. Apple has a current market value of about $960 billion.

Please contact customer service CLOSE The company's iPhone business, which drove the stock for the past 10 years, is shifting into a stable, slow growth mode. He sees iPhone revenue flat to growing 5%.
Its services business, which represents about 15% of revenue now, is likely to grow at about 15% a year for the next few years, Munster said.
Smartphone Hype Waning The hype ahead of new iPhone releases will diminish, as will obsessing over unit sales, he said. Focus will shift to the company's huge installed base of users and incremental sales of services and new products.
Its current services include the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, AppleCare, iCloud and other offerings.
The Cupertino, Calif.-based company said it expects to introduce new services. Analysts believe a subscription video-on-demand service will be one of them.
Meanwhile, Apple is working on new hardware, which could include augmented reality glasses, he said.
